name: Datatypes
description: Tattah's youngest brother, Tuftuf, is new to programming. Since his older brother is such a good programmer, his biggest dream is to outshine him. Tuftuf is a student at the German University in Cairo (GUC) where he learns to write programs in Gava. Today, Tuftuf was introduced to Gava's unsigned integer datatypes. Gava has n unsigned integer datatypes of sizes (in bits) a 1 , a 2 , ... a n . The i -th datatype have size a i bits, so it can represent every integer between 0 and 2 a i - 1 inclusive. Tuftuf is thinking of learning a better programming language. If there exists an integer x , such that x fits in some type i (in a i bits) and x · x does not fit in some other type j (in a j bits) where a i < a j , then Tuftuf will stop using Gava. Your task is to determine Tuftuf's destiny.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of Gava's unsigned integer datatypes' sizes. The second line contains a single-space-separated list of n integers ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ) — sizes of datatypes in bits. Some datatypes may have equal sizes.
output_specification: Print " YES " if Tuftuf will stop using Gava, and " NO " otherwise.
subsubtopic: 42. C++ STL Sort and Custom Comparator
approach_summary: Apply C++ STL Sort and Custom Comparator paradigm under the Basics framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
